spatial_entity.notes: City-level early modern Ottoman slavery claim. UNESCO historic-area point is a modern navigation proxy, not a slave-market or household/worksite extent.

claim.spatial_precision: greater Istanbul court and market context; no citywide prevalence surface
claim.summary: Archival specialist research on greater Istanbul between about 1590 and 1710 documents slavery as a legal and social institution, an active urban slave market, and freedom suits involving people who were legally or illegally held and sold. The candidate records a bounded urban slavery context without treating the lawsuit sample as a prevalence estimate.
claim.notes: Freedom-suit success rates and case counts are litigation evidence, not estimates of the share of Istanbul residents enslaved. Legal protections and illegal enslavement remain distinct.

territorial_practice.notes: Positive bounded urban classification. Market activity, household slavery, state slavery and illegal enslavement are not collapsed into one prevalence measure. No P-level.

source.title: Slavery, Freedom Suits, and Legal Praxis in the Ottoman Empire, ca. 1590–1710
source.geographic_scope: Greater Istanbul with Ottoman legal context
source.independence_notes: One specialist archival study using greater Istanbul court registers; the seventy-nine-suit sample is one research corpus, not seventy-nine independent prevalence votes.
source.reliability_limitations: Freedom-suit records overrepresent litigated disputes and successful plaintiffs. They demonstrate institution and legal praxis but not population prevalence.

version.version_label: Comparative Studies in Society and History 65(3), 2023, pp. 526–556

evidence.evidence_role: specialist archival evidence for urban slavery and legal praxis
evidence.locator: Article pp. 526–556; greater Istanbul sample of 79 freedom suits and discussion of urban slave markets, legal status and illegal enslavement.

geometry.resolution_method: UNESCO Sultanahmet Historic Areas coordinate used only as a modern navigation/context point for Istanbul. It is not the historic slave-market location, court locus, household/worksite distribution, or territorial practice extent.

source.title: Historic Areas of Istanbul — geographical data

geometry.notes: Navigation proxy only; no historical slavery-extent inference.
